title: Red Team Engagement — Evidence Index, SIEM Export Map & Remediation Playlist
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is the single-source index for the November 2024 Red Team engagement. It defines how evidence should be collected, named, and exported to our SIEM, maps key audit-log fields (RBAC v2 + runtime), summarizes findings we saw during the baseline run, and contains a prioritized remediation playlist with tentative owners and ETA targets.

Scope and quick notes:
- Engagement window: 2024-11-12 -> 2024-11-14 (3 days).
- Focus areas: RBAC v2 policy enforcement edges, audit-log completeness for Admin/Service tokens, SIEM ingestion for ephemeral evidence, and evidence packaging for compliance review.
- Out-of-scope: network-level red-team lateral movement beyond internal VPC, and customer data exfiltration tests (explicitly excluded).

Evidence collection and naming convention (MANDATORY):
- All artifacts MUST be dropboxed to secure evidence bucket with ACL restricted to sec-team & SRE on-call.
- Filename convention: <ENGAGEMENT>-<DAY>-<TARGET>-<TYPE>-<UTC_TS>-<SALT>
  - Example: redteam-2024-11-12-auth-service-auditlog-20241112T153400Z-3f9b.json
  - TYPES: auditlog | capture | session | config | syscall | screenshot
- For large captures (>100MB) include SHA256 digest file alongside (same name + .sha256).

Minimum audit-log schema (RBAC v2 + runtime) — required fields (compact):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- tenant_id (org id)
- principal_id (user/service id)
- principal_type (user | service | token | assumed-role)
- action (string, e.g., authorization.check, model.infer, grant.create)
- resource (ARN-style: /svc/<service>/<resource-type>/<id>)
- resource_owner (team/owner tag)
- policy_version (rbac-v2|rbac-v1)
- policy_decision (allow | deny | conditional)
- request_id (trace id)
- latency_ms (optional but recommended)
- request_payload_hash (sha256)
- response_status_code
- inference_model (optional)
- kv_cache_used (true|false)
- node_id (host/container id)
- correlated_redteam_marker (optional freeform, set by operator client)

Notes on schema: the main goal is to correlate a principal/action/resource tuple with a policy decision and a trace id so SIEM alerts can pivot to traces and evidence captures. Missing principal_type or policy_decision is a blocker for high-severity findings.

SIEM export mapping recommendations (Elastic + Splunk compatibility):
- Use top-level fields to avoid nested parsing issues. Map exactly as above.
- Add an ingest tag: ingest_source:redteam-<engagement-date>
- Add a boolean field: is_redteam=true (so we can blanket-suppress alerts during replay but still retain for post-mortem).
- Example Splunk indexed fields: timestamp, tenant_id, principal_id, action, resource, policy_decision, request_id, correlated_redteam_marker
- Recommended index lifecycle policy: 90 days hot, 1 year warm, then cold archive to s3 with encryption.

Evidence packaging for auditors (short checklist):
- For each high/critical finding include: one auditlog snippet, one session capture (if available), config snapshot, remediation diff (if applied), and a short one-paragraph narrative.
- Redaction: scrub any PII/customer payloads before packaging. Use the redaction toolchain (see linked PR).

Summary of findings from baseline run (observations, raw):
1) RBAC v2 policy_v2 fallback: several service accounts evaluated under policy_version=null where runtime returned implicit-allow. (severity: high)
   - Raw evidence: auditlog entries 20241112T16:33Z -> request_id: a3f9... (see evidence bucket).
   - Note: correlated_redteam_marker set by operator in the agent.
2) Audit log truncation on large bot requests: payload_hash missing for requests > 256k due to buffer cut-off in agent. (severity: medium)
   - Impact: reduces reproducibility for model inference escape tests.
3) SIEM ingest lag for node-level captures: node diagnostics arriving 7–12 minutes late (exceeds SLO). (severity: low)
4) Admin console: UI allowed session replay without MFA when originating IP was in a narrow range (likely static internal dev IPs). (severity: high)

Unresolved questions (to triage):
- Why are some requests missing policy_version? Is it agent-side or an authz service regression?
- Does legacy audit pipeline drop large request bodies intentionally? (we need to confirm config on audit-agent v1.3.2)

Prioritized remediation playlist (owner assignments & target dates):
- R1 (P0) — Make policy_version required in the authz decision chain (block implicit-allow).
  - Owner: Ben Cho (eng-authz)
  - Target: 2024-11-20 (code + canary)
  - Acceptance: auditlogs show policy_version != null for 100% of authz events in canary cluster for 48h.
- R2 (P0) — Immediate temporary mitigation: fail-closed for service tokens with ambiguous principal_type during red-team window.
  - Owner: Luis Moreno (sre)
  - Target: 2024-11-16 (hotfix)
- R3 (P1) — Increase audit-agent buffer threshold and add fallback to stream large payloads to s3 with pointer in log.
  - Owner: Asha Kapoor (infra)
  - Target: 2024-12-01
- R4 (P1) — Add ingestion metric and alert for SIEM lag > 3 min (per node) and pipeline retries.
  - Owner: Maya Reynolds (observability)
  - Target: 2024-11-22
- R5 (P0) — Admin console session replay: enforce MFA for any session replay request unless explicitly whitelisted via a config flag and logged.
  - Owner: Product-Security (assigned: Priya N.)
  - Target: 2024-11-25

Remediation playbook snippets (how-to/high level):
- For R1: modify authz-service to include policy_version in decision proto; add unit tests that simulate missing policy metadata; roll out on canary with 10% traffic.
- For R3: upgrade audit-agent to 1.4.0 which streams >256k payloads as multipart to s3; embed s3 pointer in request_payload_hash field until full-blob available.

Post-engagement actions (must do within 30 days):
- Full evidence package for auditors (locked, checksummed) — Owner: sec-team (Priya) — deadline 2024-12-14.
- Run a regression eval against the dev-hosted infra to ensure no adverse perf impact from streaming large payloads.
- Update internal runbooks: rbac-runbook.md, audit-log-schema.md, siem-ingest-playbook.md (linked PR referenced above).

Quick checklist for SRE/Infra on-call during replay:
- Turn on is_redteam flag on ingest nodes.
- Monitor index lag dashboards.
- If any P0s show up, create emergency incident and tag SEC-INC in Jira.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working artifact. Expect edits: sequence of ownership, ETA, and exact audit field names will be adjusted after authz-service team sync. Please annotate PRs against the linked infra PR or drop comments in the slack thread.

Appendix: quick example audit-log entry (flat JSON single-line):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-12T16:33:04Z", "tenant_id":"org-334", "principal_id":"svc-token-akk9", "principal_type":"service", "action":"authorization.check", "resource":"/svc/authz/policy/1234", "policy_version":"rbac-v2", "policy_decision":"deny", "request_id":"a3f94c2b", "latency_ms":21, "request_payload_hash":"sha256:4d2...", "node_id":"node-us-east-2-7", "is_redteam":true}

End of document.
